Q: How do conflicting rule versions, precedence and effective dates affect an eligibility explanation?
A: Relevance identifies material about the subject; applicability determines which rule governs the case. Compare jurisdiction, product, customer category, event date and effective interval, then apply an explicit precedence policy for conflicts. Publication time is not necessarily effective time, and a newer page may describe a future rule. Preserve superseded versions when historical cases need them. If necessary facts or precedence are missing, explain that uncertainty rather than allowing the generator to silently choose the most convenient passage.
Why: A claim filed in June may concern an event in April under a rule replaced in May. Selecting only the newest document can apply the wrong eligibility conditions if event date controls the policy.
Risk: Ranking score cannot settle a legal or business precedence rule.
Trade: Retrieve alternatives and resolve applicability with declared domain policy.
